summary: Created FilterExpressionException with FilterExpressionPhase (Parse/Evaluate) discriminator and Position.

Created FilterExpressionNode abstract record hierarchy: BinaryNode, UnaryNotNode, ComparisonNode, FunctionCallNode, IdentifierNode, NumberLiteralNode, StringLiteralNode + BinaryOperator/ComparisonOperator enums.

Created FilterLexer (internal): handles keywords (AND/OR/NOT case-insensitive), identifiers, decimal+integer number literals (stored as decimal), quoted strings (single/double, backslash escape), all comparison operators, parentheses.

Created FilterExpressionParser (public): recursive descent, Parse() entry point, rejects empty expressions, deferred M7/M10 identifiers (with milestone hint), unknown identifiers, incomplete AND chains, unmatched parens.
Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. All 367 tests pass. Zero new NuGet dependencies.

comments.note: FilterLexer is internal — accessible only within VideoIndexer.Core. The parser test project (WP-013) tests exclusively through FilterExpressionParser.Parse(), which is public. No InternalsVisibleTo is needed.

FilterExpressionParser.ParseArgumentList() supports only one argument (no comma support). If a future DSL function needs multiple arguments, ParseArgumentList() will need to be extended. The limitation is documented inline but not enforced with a compile-time error.

The ToComparisonOperator switch has a default branch that throws FilterExpressionException — this can only be reached if IsComparisonOperator returns true for a token type not covered by the switch, which is impossible with the current implementation. Consider removing the default branch or using a Debug.Fail() instead to document the invariant more clearly.

comments.note: FilterLexer identifier lookup uses StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase for NumericIdentifiers and FunctionIdentifiers, so 'rating >= 4' and 'RATING >= 4' would both parse correctly. This is the correct UX behaviour for a filter DSL.

ParseArgumentList supports at most one argument (no comma handling). Using a multi-arg call like 'Fn(1, 2)' would result in ',' becoming an unrecognised character in the lexer, throwing a FilterExpressionException at the lexing stage. The constraint is documented inline. Adequate for M5 scope.
Unmatched '(' with no closing ')' correctly propagates as FilterExpressionException with Phase=Parse ('Expected ) but found ... at position X'). The error message is user-friendly.

A bare number on the left side of a comparison (e.g. '5 >= Rating') is correctly rejected: the number is parsed as a primary expression, then '>=' becomes an 'Unexpected token' at the trailing-token check. The grammar enforces identifier-on-left semantics without special-casing.
No issues found — parser and lexer implementation is clean, consistent, and well-structured.

summary: Code review PASS. All five Filtering/ files reviewed line-by-line. No blocking issues found.
FilterToken.cs: 16 token types correctly cover the full M5 grammar. FilterExpressionException.cs: Phase discriminator and Position fields are correctly designed.
FilterExpressionNode.cs: Clean sealed record hierarchy. All node types correct and immutable. FunctionCallNode uses IReadOnlyList for arguments.

FilterLexer.cs: Case-insensitive keywords via ToUpperInvariant, InvariantCulture decimal parsing, backslash escape in string literals, unterminated string detection — all correct. Correctly marked internal.

FilterExpressionParser.cs: Recursive descent with correct precedence. Deferred M7/M10 identifier rejection with milestone hints is clean. Trailing-token check prevents silent partial parses. Empty expression guard via AsSpan().Trim().IsEmpty is efficient.

comments.note: FilterLexer and FilterExpressionParser are well-structured. Recursive descent grammar precedence (OR < AND < NOT < primary) is correct and documented in the XML remarks. Advance() safely stops at Eof, preventing out-of-bounds. No issues found.

ToComparisonOperator default branch throws FilterExpressionException (Phase=Parse) for an unreachable code path. This conflates a programming error with a user expression error. Using InvalidOperationException or Debug.Assert would better document the 'this should never happen' invariant. This is a behavioral change so not applied as Fix-Forward. Already flagged by Developer.

NumericIdentifiers and FunctionIdentifiers are disjoint identifier sets, but ParseIdentifierExpression dispatches on the next token ('(' vs. comparison op) without enforcing which set the identifier belongs to. A numeric identifier like 'Rating' followed by '(' would parse as FunctionCallNode('Rating', []). The evaluator (WP-006) will type-check this. Intentionally permissive at the parser level.
FilterLexer.LexNumber allows a trailing decimal point (e.g. '5.' parses as 5m via decimal.TryParse). This is acceptable behavior for a filter DSL and consistent with .NET decimal parsing semantics.
